record.context_brief: Two-machine flow shop with proportional-linear operations
record.original_question: Given a two-machine flow shop in which each job has one operation on each machine and operation i of job j has proportional-linear time-dependent processing time p_ij(t) = b_ij(a + b t) when it starts at time t, with common constants a and b and operation-specific coefficient b_ij, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or can it be solved in polynomial time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-machine flow shop scheduling problem defined as follows. There are n jobs, indexed by j = 1, ..., n, and two machines M_1 and M_2. Each job j consists of two operations: operation (1, j) must be processed on M_1 and operation (2, j) on M_2, with the usual flow-shop precedence requiring that operation (2, j) cannot start before operation (1, j) completes. Each machine processes at most one operation at a time, and operations cannot be preempted.

The processing times are time-dependent and proportional-linear: there are fixed real constants a > 0 and b > 0, common to all operations, and for every operation (i, j) (i ∈ {1, 2}) there is a job- and machine-specific positive coefficient b_{ij} such that if operation (i, j) starts at time t ≥ 0, then its processing time is

    p_{ij}(t) = b_{ij}(a + b t).

All jobs are available at time 0. Let C_j denote the completion time of job j on M_2 in a given schedule. The objective is to find a schedule minimizing the total completion time Σ_{j=1}^{n} C_j.

Determine the computational complexity of this problem. Specifically, is it NP-hard (at least in the ordinary sense), or is there a polynomial-time algorithm that solves it to optimality?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not produce a definitive complexity classification for the two-machine flow-shop problem F2 | p_{ij} = b_{ij}(a+bt) | ΣC_j. Related variants (e.g., linear deterioration p_{ij} = a_{ij} + b_{ij}t with makespan objective, or proportional deterioration with weighted completion time) have known NP-hardness or polynomial-time results, but the specific proportional-linear ΣC_j case with two machines does not appear to have a published, conclusive resolution. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Solution algorithms for the total weighted completion time minimization flow shop scheduling with decreasing linear deterioration
status_evidence.snippet: Studies related flow-shop problems with linear deterioration and total (weighted) completion time, but does not settle F2|p_{ij}=b_{ij}(a+bt)|ΣC_j.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related but distinct problem; complexity of the exact stated problem not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Minimizing Total Completion Time in a Two-Machine Flowshop: Analysis of Special Cases
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes special cases of two-machine flow shop with total completion time, classical (time-independent) processing times.
status_evidence.claim: Does not address proportional-linear time-dependent processing times.
